# Project Governance 3.0.0-rc.10.8

Governed reviews can use compact context packets while retaining large local routing records.
Normal checks can finish cleanly when a recorded build helper shuts down shortly after its parent.

- Give generated context records one shared 32 MiB write/read allowance. Keep actual model input
  compact and preserve source, workspace, policy and required-guidance checks. Optional original
  freshness uses the existing 16 MiB source declaration rather than the smaller narrative default.
- Report invalid prepared context separately from changed approval. A refusal before native model
  launch no longer invalidates that model's qualification. Corrective edits still require fresh
  current-source review context; no stale continuation is accepted.
- Observe recorded detached descendants finishing within the existing termination grace. Confirm
  cleanup only after full process inspection establishes absence. Missing inspection, changed
  identity or a still-live helper keeps the outcome unknown; no checker replay is introduced.
- Admit `check-reconcile` and `check-output` through the managed write path. Recovery still verifies
  exact identity and cleanup, releases only the stopped check's reader, and preserves original
  failed results and unrelated reservations.
- Clarify native consultation and existing-conversation workspace alignment. A runtime upgrade
  does not reattach a host conversation to another worktree or require a whole-app restart.

This is an operator-authorized manual release using completed local qualification. Hosted CI is
skipped. Focused source regressions, type checking, compiled installation, greenfield entry and
managed recovery proof passed. The installed native-provider cases use deterministic fixtures;
this patch does not claim fresh live-model, physical-device or accepted-task efficiency proof.

Adopter upgrades remain deliberate. Retry the affected complete normal gate after installation;
the release does not waive hooks, renew project proof declarations, reset spending or enable
delegation. No adopter files are changed by publication.
